findings.title: Loss of traceID in log output
findings.body: The previous implementation added a `traceID` field via `tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)` to the log parameters. This logic was removed in the refactor and not replicated in the new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` (which only adds endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname). As a result, plugin request logs no longer contain the trace ID, which is a regression in observability/debuggability compared to before.

findings.title: Logger name still references old 'instrumentation' terminology
findings.body: `log.New("plugin.instrumentation")` passed to `NewLoggerMiddleware` still uses the old "instrumentation" name even though the whole point of this PR is to rename instrumentation middleware to metrics middleware and separate out logging concerns. This leaves inconsistent/outdated naming in log output that doesn't reflect the renamed middleware architecture.

findings.title: Missing nil-request guards unlike sibling middlewares
findings.body: Other middlewares (e.g. LoggerMiddleware, MetricsMiddleware) check `if req == nil` before accessing req.PluginContext to avoid potential nil pointer dereference. ContextualLoggerMiddleware.QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics do not perform this check before calling instrumentContext(ctx, endpoint, req.PluginContext), so a nil req would panic here, whereas it would be gracefully handled further down the middleware chain in LoggerMiddleware.

findings.title: Test name not updated to match renamed middleware
findings.body: The test function is still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware even though the file was renamed to metrics_middleware_test.go and the production type/constructor renamed to MetricsMiddleware/newMetricsMiddleware. This is inconsistent with the stated goal of the PR (better naming/consistency) and could confuse future readers correlating test names with implementation names.
